title: The effect of semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly on energy intake, appetite, control of eating, and gastric emptying in adults with obesity
authors: Friedrichsen M, Breitschaft A, Tadayon S, Wizert A, Skovgaard D
population: Adults with obesity, randomised to semaglutide escalated to 2.4 mg weekly or placebo, double-blind
funder: This study was funded by Novo Nordisk A/S; medical writing was funded by Novo Nordisk A/S. Four authors are Novo Nordisk employees; the fifth is employed by Parexel, paid by Novo Nordisk to assist in conducting the study; the sponsor generated the randomisation schedule.
result: Ad libitum lunch energy intake was 35% lower on semaglutide (1736 against 2676 kJ; difference -940 kJ). Hunger and prospective food consumption fell and fullness and satiety rose; food cravings were fewer and weaker. Weight fell 9.9% against 0.4%. Gastric emptying measured indirectly by paracetamol absorption after a standardised breakfast: AUC over 0 to 5 h was 8% higher on semaglutide (P = 0.005), not significant after correction for body weight, with no effect on 0 to 1 h AUC; the authors report no evidence of delayed gastric emptying at week 20.
